entries.title: Render live financial wiring and Pages publishing fix
entries.why: This improves day-to-day operation: render live financial wiring and pages publishing fix.
entries.what: **Render live financial deployment path**: added render.yaml (Node web service + PostgreSQL 16), idempotent finance:bootstrap pre-deploy step, and environment-configured HTTPS payment/card/source adapters wired into the durable financial runtime. **Pages workflow fix**: root cause of the failed Pages runs was actions/configure-pages with enablement: true trying to create a Pages site with a token that can deploy but not create (Resource not accessible by integration). The workflow now preflights the Pages API, removes the forbidden auto-create attempt, assembles via tools/demo-site.mjs, and publishes after pushes/successful What's New runs. If Pages is not enabled yet it warns and skips instead of leaving main red. **CI**: native PostgreSQL job now exercises finance:bootstrap idempotence and environment-mismatch refusal. **Docs/evidence**: docs/31-RENDER-LIVE-OPERATIONS.md, updated financial contract status, reports/FIN-RENDER-0001/verification.md, ledger rows.
entries.whatYouNeedToDo: No action required. Open the named area if you want to see the change in place.

entries.title: Financial completion: durable book, demo safety and approval gates (high risk)
entries.why: PR #46 merged incomplete, high-risk financial groundwork while its What's New entry implied low risk/no action. Issue #47 still has no authorized charge rates, approval provenance, or authoritative legacy distribution source. This PR makes the demo/durable boundary explicit, adds a PostgreSQL-backed financial book with atomic/idempotent commands and approval gates, and corrects the shipped What's New record. It does **not** approve live financial use.
entries.what: Demo safety: financial demo POSTs require Idempotency-Key; listed demo financial mutations run through an order-preserving snapshot/rollback wrapper; authenticated legacy financial mutations are refused unless PORTAL_ALLOW_DEMO=1 is explicit; batch output is labelled simulated-posted with no voucher reference. Durable financial book: private PostgreSQL schema, checksummed explicit migrations, empty-book init, singleton row-lock unit of work, append-only command receipts, replay/key-conflict detection, integrity/reconciliation pre-checks, and pre-commit rollback. /finance/* never falls back to the demo world. Financial service: role gates; provider/source checks before evidence parsing; verified cash before allocation; scoped/effective-dated rules; durable P1 configuration requests with null rates; second-person approval (self-approval refused); monthly catch-up scheduler with versioned keys; read-only statement/reconciliation/configuration views; round-up provider-token gates. Policy/statement correctness: distribution validation/evidence helpers, structured new policy IDs without rewriting existing IDs, inception-to-current fund history with missing NAV unavailable, and separately recorded recommendations displayed for 5 seconds. Evidence/ops: docs/30-FINANCIAL-COMPLETION-CONTRACT.md, reports/FIN-COMPLETION-0001/verification.md, ledger rows, finance migration/init CLIs, and a…
entries.whatYouNeedToDo: Owner approval to merge is recorded on this PR. **Do not deploy live or enable live financial operations** until issue #47 authorized rates/provenance and legacy source records, approved provider/source adapters and credentials, backup/restore, and operational scheduler qualification are supplied. Demo fixtures are synthetic only.

entries.title: Unit-linked statements and round-up demo (work in progress)
entries.why: PR #46 was merged while still marked work in progress. Its shipped What's New entry understated the risk and implied no operator action. This correction records what actually shipped and what remains unsafe/incomplete.
entries.what: Shipped unit-linked statement/history and a time-limited recorded recommendation display, plus simulated round-up settings/preview. These are demo surfaces, not live bank integration or tokenisation. Shipped a calendar-only monthly anniversary calculator and distribution capture/backfill groundwork. The batch remained a simulation; no durable scheduler or postings were shipped. The follow-up financial completion work (durable PostgreSQL book, atomic/idempotent commands, configuration requests/approval, scheduler, provider gates, legacy mutation lockdown) is tracked in the financial completion PR and docs/30-FINANCIAL-COMPLETION-CONTRACT.md. It is not approved for live use by this entry.
entries.whatYouNeedToDo: Treat PR #46 as high-risk, incomplete financial groundwork. Do not enable live payments, round-up collection, batch posting, or charge configuration from it. Use only explicitly identified demo/test fixtures. Read docs/30-FINANCIAL-COMPLETION-CONTRACT.md and issue #47; obtain approved rates/source records, independent verification, and Raheel Atta's approval of the exact tested commit before any live financial use.

entries.title: Move browser credentials to a session cookie, add headers and guards
entries.why: The console kept an operator's access token in sessionStorage/localStorage and rebuilt an Authorization: Bearer header from it on every call (src/ui/api.ts:19, src/ui/partner-portal.tsx:200). Anything able to run script in the page — one XSS bug, or one compromised front-end dependency in a single 2.2 MB bundle — could read that token and post it anywhere. It is a static value from PORTAL_AUTH_TOKENS with no expiry and no server-side revocation, so a leak is permanent until every token is rotated.
entries.what: **Tier A — the credential leaves the browser's reach.** src/server/auth.ts: a SessionStore of opaque 256-bit ids (stored as SHA-256 digests, 12 h TTL, capped) and POST /api/session / DELETE /api/session in src/server/main.ts. The browser exchanges the token **once** for __Host-portal_session=…; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=43200. Sign-out revokes the session server-side *and* clears the cookie with identical attributes. src/ui/api.ts: stops reading the token, purges the legacy key from sessionStorage **and** localStorage once on load, sends credentials: 'same-origin' (never include), and carries the status on ApiError so a 401 returns the operator to the sign-in form instead of a dead console. src/ui/partner-portal.tsx: the token form now signs in; a "Sign out" control ends the session. **CSRF, because a cookie is ambient.** SameSite=Lax is not a defence on its own, so every unsafe method on a cookie-authenticated request is also Origin (fallback Referer) checked against the request host and PORTAL_CORS_ORIGIN; Origin: null is refused. The mandatory custom header stays, so Bearer callers keep their incidental preflight protection. Machine clients are unchanged. SameSite=Lax, not Strict: the portal is linked from external systems and Strict would arrive logged out. **Tier B — defence in depth, set in one place.** src/server/security.ts, used by sendBuffer() s…
entries.whatYouNeedToDo: Review the change with your data-protection owner, rotate any affected secret from your secret store, and re-validate the connection before the next sync.

entries.title: Publish release notes automatically from PRs
entries.why: Release notes were curated by hand. A merged PR (#38) shipped without an entry, PR #39 was only a correction, and the What's New tab explicitly told operators that merging a PR does nothing. Maintaining the seed, rebuilding the offline demo and committing the generated files is a manual three-step ritual that gets forgotten.
entries.what: .github/workflows/whats-new.yml reacts to pull_request_target (opened / edited / synchronize / reopened / closed), push on main, and workflow_dispatch backfill. It checks out **main only** — never PR code — verifies the full build, then commits the regenerated feed and offline demo to main. tools/whats-new-sync.mjs + domain drafters in src/core/whatsnew.ts turn PR title, labels and ## Why / ## What changed / ## What you need to do sections into an operator-facing note. One stable WN-PR-‹n› entry per PR: proposed on open, shipped with the merge date on merge, removed on unmerged close. PR text is sanitised to bounded plain text before it reaches generated code, HTML or the console. backlog/whats-new-auto.json (source of truth) and generated src/core/whatsnew.auto.ts feed the registry, API and static demo. A lastMergedAt watermark backfill and proposed-entry re-check self-heal failed or missed runs; whats-new:skip / whats-new:include control eligibility. UI badges proposed entries as "in review — not shipped" and links to the PR. CI and npm run whats-new:check fail if the two committed files drift. Docs: new decision record docs/28-AUTOMATIC-WHATS-NEW.md, updated docs/13-…, README, CONTRIBUTING, backlog chunk and ledger row.
entries.whatYouNeedToDo: Write PR bodies with the three headings above — they become the release note. Label internal/tooling PRs whats-new:skip. Enable **Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → Read and write** (or set a WHATS_NEW_TOKEN secret) so the workflow can commit to main. No manual What's New edit is needed.
